questions.question: Which language should the school website and portal use?
questions.rationale: The inspected application is Laravel 12 and already uses PHP.

options.label: PHP
options.description: Keep the existing Laravel application and its server-rendered Blade pages.

questions.question: Which framework should power the school website and portal?
questions.rationale: Preserve the existing Laravel 12 framework rather than replacing it with an unrelated API framework.

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Use Azure Functions for a serverless API; this is not the existing framework.

questions.question: Confirm or refine the extension scope. In particular: should timetables be uploaded files or structured schedule entries (the database already has timetable_entries); should attendance be recorded online by authorized staff or imported/uploaded (attendance_records already exists); should report cards be uploaded files or published from structured exam/report data (report_cards and exam_results already exist); which roles may manage admissions, timetables, attendance, and report cards; and which academic years/terms must be supported?
questions.answer: Keep the public admissions application; add staff-managed timetable, attendance, and report-card workflows using the existing academic-year/term and school-record foundations. Prefer structured timetable and attendance records and structured report-card data unless the school confirms file uploads are required. Define role permissions for administrator, admissions officer, teacher, non-teaching staff, and student, and retain academic-year/term scoping. The website must reflect live records from the existing configured database; preserve its current connection and schema, and do not replace live data with static or mock content.
questions.rationale: Existing migrations and the README establish the data foundations, but do not determine the desired authoring/upload workflow, role permissions, or academic-year policy. The user additionally confirmed that the website must display live data from the existing configured database.
questions.recommendedChoice: Keep the public admissions application; add staff-managed timetable, attendance, and report-card workflows using the existing academic-year/term and school-record foundations. Prefer structured timetable and attendance records and structured report-card data unless the school confirms file uploads are required. Define role permissions for administrator, admissions officer, teacher, non-teaching staff, and student, and retain academic-year/term scoping.

questions.question: Which data stores should the school website use? Select every required store. Choose “No datastore required” only if there is no database or file storage.
questions.rationale: The existing app requires relational persistence. Blob Storage is recommended because report-card upload is requested, while the exact file workflows are to be confirmed.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Only for an app that does not save records or files.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: Keep the existing documented default relational database for school records.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Use a managed relational database for school records.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Use Azure SQL for relational school records.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store and serve timetable or report-card files if file uploads are confirmed.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use school application features?
questions.rationale: The existing portal already uses authenticated email/password accounts and role-based access.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users authenticate before accessing student and staff portal features.

options.label: No
options.description: Application features are available without user sign-in.

questions.question: How should students securely access attendance, timetables, and report cards? A student number alone is guessable and must not grant access to private student records. Confirm whether students should use a secure account/login, or student number plus an additional verification factor.
questions.answer: Require an authenticated student account with authorization bound to that student's own record; do not treat the student number alone as authentication.
questions.rationale: The existing login uses email/password, and students have a unique admission_number with an optional linked user account; the requested access method needs confirmation.
questions.recommendedChoice: Require an authenticated student account with authorization bound to that student's own record; do not treat the student number alone as authentication.
